title.narrative: More productive and competitive SMEs and MNEs contribute to and provide sustainable and decent employment, including a just transition to environmental sustainability

description.narrative: The decade following the global financial crisis has witnessed a consistent decline in productivity growth, a development that has been compounded by the COVID-19 pandemic. This trend is of particular concern to most emerging and developing economies including Ghana. The contribution of structural transformation (i.e., labour reallocation towards higher-productivity sectors as well as within-sector transformation) to productivity growth has slowed down and integration in national and regional value chains has decreased. Sustaining productivity growth in an economy is a complex process as there are many contributing factors to consider at national, sector and enterprise-level. Therefore, the ILO promotes an ecosystems approach to identify the most pressing constraints to productivity growth and the level at which they can be addressed. Through consultation between Governments, Employers and workers organizations, the programme selects a “slice” of the economy such as specific sectors and associated businesses which have a high potential for productivity growth and decent job creation. The Srtategy of the intervention is to promote inclusive growth and decent work through policy development, data collection and analysis, training, study tours, peer learning. In addtion, the it supports the revision of relevant national labour legislation and implementing interventions addressing constraints to productivity growth and decent work in the textile and garment and the shea processing sectors.
